Messages.Author: Daneel
Messages.Body:
"Orpheus" <orph...@DEADSPAMfree.fr> wrote in message news:<401bca15$0$2952$626a...@news.free.fr>...


That's not necessarily foolish. You cannot force players into making
decisions this way. The reason is more than simple. You at any given
point can break any deal you make. Your "reputation" (behaviour at
previous games, which games have no bearing on any other games by
nature) has no impact on any current deals you offer or accept.
Therefor by legally accepting the possibility of "enforcing" such a
deal you could bully the table and sweep in an unsportsmanlike manner.

Bye,

Daneel



How can you say such a thing when there are no rules about deals or
deal breaking? As far as I interpret, every player MUST play to
maximise their vp. What Orpheus has pointed out is a loop hole. Since
there are NO rules on deal making but there are VEKN rules concerning
maximising vp, you could argue that the play did not attempt to
maximise his vp. If the player about to be outed has nothing to lose.
So why not take a deal?

When will the VEKN make clear rules on deal making? There are grey
areas... not all players and judges are clear on situations like this.
From what I can tell there are cases where the guidelines have been
applied incorrectly. I understand that politics is the essense of the
game but... there are loop holes where conclusion can inflitrate into
the game.

Andrew Daley

The V:EKN does't force a decision over another of equal "play to win"

>
> When will the VEKN make clear rules on deal making? There are grey

Sometime back there. I forget when it was all clarified as much as
anything so inherently judgement-requiring can be.

For those who have missed it:

1) Play to win.
2) If you can't win, play to maximize your VPs.

Deals are not enforced or mandated by any rules.
It is legal to honor a deal if the terms of the deal (if honored) represent
"playing to win" at the time the deal was made, even if the subsequent
decision to honor the deal when the time comes doesn't maximize one's
chance to win to maximize one's VP intake.

dal...@iinet.net.au (Andrew Daley) wrote in message news:<8821ff0a.04013...@posting.google.com>...

> Damnans <damna...@ono.com> wrote in message news:<401BC183...@ono.com>...
> > Orpheus wrote:
> > >
> > > A player is about to die painfully. You offer him 1 VP if he does, or
> > > doesn't do, something. You don't especially have a breakdealing reputation,
> > > or have quite the contrary. Does he have the right to refuse ?
> >
> > A player cannot be forced into a deal, so he or she has the right
> > to refuse that deal.
> >
>
> How can you say such a thing when there are no rules about deals or
> deal breaking? As far as I interpret, every player MUST play to
> maximise their vp. What Orpheus has pointed out is a loop hole. Since
> there are NO rules on deal making but there are VEKN rules concerning
> maximising vp, you could argue that the play did not attempt to
> maximise his vp. If the player about to be outed has nothing to lose.
> So why not take a deal?

Tournament rules recognising deals is a one-way phenomenon. The rules
the game is built upon (VTES rules) say nothing about deals (don't
even recognise deals).

Tournament rules say that you must play _according to the VTES rules_
with the goal of maximising VPs. The only exception to not be
currently playing to maximise your VPs is to honor a legally made deal
which at the time of making served to maximise your VPs. There is only
this way, and no other way around.

> When will the VEKN make clear rules on deal making? There are grey
> areas... not all players and judges are clear on situations like this.
> From what I can tell there are cases where the guidelines have been
> applied incorrectly. I understand that politics is the essense of the
> game but... there are loop holes where conclusion can inflitrate into
> the game.
>
> Andrew Daley

No loopholes exist regarding this topic. The rules - VTES and VEKN -
are pretty clear I think.

Since nothing forces you to keep a deal nothing in the rules can force
you to make one.

Bye,

Daneel
